coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Building 102 (former Power House)
record.summary: The 1912 Classical Revival powerhouse on 20th Street between Buildings 101 and 104, designed by Charles Peter Weeks, which generated compressed air and distributed electricity for the shipyard and still housed BAE Systems' electrical service when rehabilitation began. Orton rebuilt it as office space with a mezzanine and a rear addition (about 15,300-18,000 sq ft) and subleased it to JUUL Labs for ten years; the current occupant is unknown.

notes.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprint -- high confidence in the outline itself. This footprint's area (~1955 m2 / ~21,043 sqft) is roughly double the '11,266 sf' figure this project's own earlier research attached to 'Building 102 (former Compressor House)' -- that figure was not independently re-verified this pass, and could describe interior/leasable area rather than the full building footprint, or could itself be imprecise. Flagging this discrepancy rather than silently picking one number; treat the footprint geometry (real, surveyed) as more reliable than the previously-cited sqft figure.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This parcel (blklot 4046001) has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll. The real Assessor lot groups 5 named buildings into one polygon with no further official subdivision -- this feature uses the real building footprint instead, extracted and matched individually.
notes.regulatory_context: The former Power House, built 1912, part of the same 20th Street Historic Core rehabilitation by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) as Building 101 (HPC packet 2013.1168E, Nov 26 2013 review). Per that packet, Building 102 was 'in fairly good condition' at the time and in use as the powerhouse facility. No confirmed real-world tenant identified by any source found.

facts.value: Orton Development, Inc. through Historic Pier 70, LLC (66-year master lease L-15814 from the Port of San Francisco)
Marcy Wong Donn Logan Architects (design architect); Mark Hulbert, Preservation Architecture (historic architect)

Developer equity up to $14 million plus loans; Port participation rent of 50% of revenues above debt and a 14% equity return; sources in 2018: Port capital $1.8M, Seismic Safety Loan $23.6M, historic tax credit equity $20.4M, private debt and equity $81.2M
Contributing resource to the Union Iron Works Historic District (NRHP, listed April 17, 2014)
Tall rectangular concrete building with hipped mission-tile roof, five arched bays, terra cotta shell frieze and copper cornice
128 ft 6 in by 42 ft 4 in by 48 ft tall
8,428 (NRHP, first floor and basement); 11,266 before and 15,331 after rehabilitation (Port 2019 Table 1); 15,500 original and just over 18,000 after per Retrofit magazine
Office (subleased to JUUL Labs, 10-year term, entire building less the Port's basement electrical room)
JUUL Labs subleased Building 102 (and 104); the presence of an e-cigarette maker on Port land drew public objection in 2018-2019
Powerhouse No. 1 Electric: offices, four air compressors, three rotary converters, switchboard and transformers on the main floor; still serving some of BAE Systems' electrical needs in 2013
'Building 102 key historic features' listed by the Port as publicly accessible
